s: Which Newspaper strongly supported the Horne Rule Movernent in Andhra
x:
The newspaper Andhra Mata strongly supported the Home Rule Movement launched by Annie Besant. It published articles advocating self- government, political rights and nationalist ideals, thereby creating awareness among the Telugu-speaking people. Newspapers played a crucial role in spreading the message of the Home Rule Movement throughout Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is

s: "No Pullari (Grass) Tax" Movement was led in Palanadu by
x:
The No Pullari (Grass Tax) Movement was one of the important peasant agitations in the Andhra region during the freedom struggle. It was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu in the Palanadu region of Guntur district. The British Government imposed a Pullari Tax, a tax collected from villagers for allowing their cattle to graze in forest lands. This tax severely affected poor farmers and cattle rearers whose livelihood depended on grazing rights. Kanneganti Hanumanthu organized the villagers and refused to pay the unjust tax. His courageous resistance made him a symbol of peasant protest against British oppression. During the agitation, British police opened fire, and Kanneganti Hanumanthu was martyred in 1922. His sacrifice inspired subsequent peasant movements in Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who is popularly known as 'Andhra Shivaji'?
x:
Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary was a prominent freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh who actively participated in the Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement during the Non-Cooperation Movement. He displayed exceptional courage, organizational ability and patriotism in mobilizing peasants against British rule. His fearless leadership, military discipline and determination in resisting the British reminded people of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Because of his bravery and leadership qualities, he came to be popularly known as "Andhra Shivaji." He organized volunteers, encouraged people not to pay taxes and played a key role in sustaining the movement despite severe repression by the colonial government.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: When did the Palnadu Pullari Satyagraha take place?
x:
The Palnadu Pullari Satyagraha (1921–22) was a peasant agitation against the British- imposed Pullari (grazing tax) in the Palnadu region. The movement protested restrictions on grazing rights and forest usage imposed by the colonial government. It became one of the important peasant movements associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Identify the person who was the president of the National College founded at Machilipatnamin 1910
x:
The National College at Machilipatnam, established in 1910, was founded to promote national education free from British influence. Nyapati Subbarao served as its President. The institution became an important centre for nationalist thought and produced many students who later participated in India's freedom movement.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
